7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. underestimate

I think the A arguments are mathematically correct for the population-average incidence reduction, but they are answering a different question than the one asked.

With an all-or-nothing mechanism the biological effect per exposure event is binary. For the p fraction that is rendered completely non-susceptible the risk per infectious contact is zero, i.e. 100% per-exposure reduction. For the 1-p fraction the risk per contact is identical to unvaccinated, i.e. 0% reduction. That is the mechanistic per-exposure efficacy.

The incidence rate ratio is a cohort-level, calendar-time average. 
IR_v = Events_v / PT_v with Events_v generated only by the 1-p susceptible sub-fraction and PT_v = p·T + (1-p)·susceptible person-time. The p completely protected individuals contribute immortal person-time with no events. That immortal person-time is a statistical feature of averaging over the whole vaccinated cohort, not a change in the per-contact risk of someone who remains susceptible.

Hence 1 - IRR = p is the population-mixed average reduction in incidence rate, the mean of 100% in responders and 0% in non-responders, diluted further by averaging over follow-up as the 1-p susceptible fraction is depleted. The instantaneous hazard in the still-susceptible vaccinated is h_v(t) = λ(1-p) e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}], which declines with t only because susceptibles are being removed, not because the per-exposure risk conditional on being susceptible changes. The per-exposure risk conditional on remaining at risk stays λ for the 1-p fraction and 0 for the p fraction for all t.

The rate-based VE is therefore a conservative, person-time diluted proxy for the biological per-exposure effect operating at the moment of exposure. It sits below the 100% reduction actually realized in the responder sub-group and is pulled toward the null by the mixing of 0% and 100% effects and by the growing immortal denominator. In the rare disease / short follow-up limit the dilution disappears and the rate ratio recovers p, but for any realistic follow-up the time-averaged rate reduction underestimates the conditional per-exposure efficacy that the vaccine exerts on a contact in an individual who can still be infected.

That is why the rate ratio is often described as a population incidence reduction, while the true per-exposure, per-contact biological efficacy is the complete 100% protection in the responders, which the population average p, and hence 1-IRR, underestimates.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: B. underestimate

The key is what we mean by “per-exposure”. In an all-or-nothing model the biological effect per infectious contact is binary.

With protected fraction p and susceptible fraction 1-p

* responder: per-exposure risk = 0, per-exposure VE = 100 %
* non-responder: per-exposure risk = π0, per-exposure VE = 0 %

The average per-exposure VE across the whole vaccinated cohort is p×100% + (1-p)×0% = p, that is the population proportion protected. That is the same quantity as 1-RRcum = p and it is constant with time because the per-exposure risk of the 1-p susceptible sub-fraction does not change.

1-IRR is a cohort-level, time-averaged rate reduction,
VEIR = 1 – Events_v/PT_v ÷ Events_u/PT_u.

The vaccinated person-time denominator PT_v = N[pT + (1-p)(1-e^{-λT})/λ] keeps accumulating immortal person-time from the p completely protected individuals who can never generate an event, while the numerator is generated only by the 1-p susceptible sub-fraction. The estimator therefore returns the population-mixed mean p, averaged over responders and non-responders and over calendar time as the susceptible vaccinated are depleted.

That population mean is by construction a dilution of the biological per-exposure effect that is actually operating at the moment of an exposure in a person who can still be infected. Conditional on remaining at risk, the hazard in the susceptible vaccinated is the same as in unvaccinated, and conditional on being a responder the hazard is zero. The rate-based VE is the conservative, time-averaged proxy for the conditional per-exposure biological effect, mixing 100% protection in responders with 0% in non-responders.

In the short follow-up/rare disease limit λT≪1 the time-averaging disappears and VEIR→p, which is why the cumulative risk ratio is often quoted as the proportion protected. For realistic follow-up the rate-based estimate remains a population average that sits below the 100% per-exposure protection realized in the responder sub-group. That is the classic mixture interpretation: 1-IRR = p is the average reduction in population incidence, and it underestimates the magnitude of the per-exposure biological efficacy that is 100% in the protected fraction. For a leaky vaccine HR(t)=1-VEpe is constant and 1-IRR recovers the per-exposure effect; for a genuinely all-or-nothing vaccine it does not.

The all-or-nothing model is a mixture and that mixture matters for what we mean by “per-exposure”.

Let p be the fraction rendered completely immune and 1-p be phenotypically unvaccinated with constant force of infection λ. Then

An incidence rate ratio is a cohort-level, time-averaged quantity

IR_u=λ

* responders: per-exposure risk =0, per-exposure VE=100%
* non-responders: per-exposure risk = λ, per-exposure VE=0%

It is the average reduction in incidence rate across the whole vaccinated cohort, averaged over responders and non-responders and over calendar time, with the denominator constantly inflated by the immortal person-time of the p completely protected who will never contribute an event.

The population rate reduction sits below the 100% per-exposure protection realised in responders.

For a leaky vaccine HR(t) is constant and 1-IRR recovers the per-exposure VE; for a genuine all-or-nothing vaccine the rate-based estimator is a conservative null-biased average of the 0% and 100% effects.

IR_v = Events_v / PT_v

B. underestimate

The disagreement is definitional, not mathematical. In an all-or-nothing model the vaccinated cohort is a mixture of p individuals with per-exposure risk 0 and 1-p individuals who are phenotypically identical to unvaccinated. Conditional on an exposure occurring in a host who is still able to be infected, the biological per-exposure efficacy is 100% in the responder fraction and 0% in the non-responder fraction. The population mean of that 100%/0% mixture is p, which is what people usually quote as the proportion protected.

1 – IRR is a cohort-level, time-averaged rate reduction: Events_v / PT_v divided by Events_u / PT_u. The PT_v denominator keeps accumulating immortal person-time from the p fraction who will never generate an event, while the numerator is generated only by the 1-p susceptible sub-fraction. That person-time dilution makes 1-IRR a population-mixed, calendar-time average of the two sub-groups.

The decreasing instantaneous hazard h_v(t)=λ(1-p)e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}] and the result 1-IRR(T)=pλT/[pλT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})] ≥ p are real, but they describe the relationship between a time-averaged rate ratio and the cumulative risk ratio 1-RRcum=p. They do not describe a change in the per-exposure risk of an individual who remains susceptible. Depletion of the 1-p susceptible fraction over follow-up lowers the average hazard in the whole vaccinated cohort, it does not lower the per-exposure risk per contact in those who are still susceptible.

Hence 1-IRR = p in the rare-disease/short follow-up limit is the population-averaged incidence reduction. It averages the 100% biological per-exposure effect in responders with the 0% effect in non-responders and averages over all calendar person-time, including the immortal person-time contributed by the completely protected p fraction. In that mechanistic, conditional-on-exposure sense the population rate reduction is a conservative, null-biased proxy for the 100% per-exposure protection that is actually operating during an exposure in the protected sub-group. That is the usual reason the rate-based VE is described as diluted relative to the true per-exposure biological effect under an all-or-nothing mechanism, and it is why the rate ratio is treated as underestimating the per-contact efficacy once you condition on being at risk.

h_v(t)=λ(1-p)e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}],  HR(t)=h_v/h_u=(1-p)e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}]

IRR(T)=(1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]/[pλT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})] <1-p,

1-IRR(T)=pλT/[pλT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})] ≥ p,

is Events_v/PT_v divided by Events_u/PT_u. That population mean p is the average reduction in incidence rate across the whole vaccinated cohort, and it is by construction a dilution of the 100% per-exposure biological effect operating in the responder sub-group. It is the average of 100% efficacy in responders and 0% in non-responders. B. underestimate

I think the A arguments are mathematically correct for the population-average incidence reduction, but they are answering a different question than the one asked.

With an all-or-nothing mechanism the biological effect per exposure event is binary. For the p fraction that is rendered completely non-susceptible the risk per infectious contact is zero, i.e. 100% per-exposure reduction. For the 1-p fraction the risk per contact is identical to unvaccinated, i.e. 0% reduction. That is the mechanistic per-exposure efficacy.

The incidence rate ratio is a cohort-level, calendar-time average. 
IR_v = Events_v / PT_v with Events_v generated only by the 1-p susceptible sub-fraction and PT_v = p·T + (1-p)·susceptible person-time. The p completely protected individuals contribute immortal person-time with no events. That immortal person-time is a statistical feature of averaging over the whole vaccinated cohort, not a change in the per-contact risk of someone who remains susceptible.

Hence 1 - IRR = p is the population-mixed average reduction in incidence rate, the mean of 100% in responders and 0% in non-responders, diluted further by averaging over follow-up as the 1-p susceptible fraction is depleted. The instantaneous hazard in the still-susceptible vaccinated is h_v(t) = λ(1-p) e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}], which declines with t only because susceptibles are being removed, not because the per-exposure risk conditional on being susceptible changes. The per-exposure risk conditional on remaining at risk stays λ for the 1-p fraction and 0 for the p fraction for all t.

The rate-based VE is therefore a conservative, person-time diluted proxy for the biological per-exposure effect operating at the moment of exposure. It sits below the 100% reduction actually realized in the responder sub-group and is pulled toward the null by the mixing of 0% and 100% effects and by the growing immortal denominator. In the rare disease / short follow-up limit the dilution disappears and the rate ratio recovers p, but for any realistic follow-up the time-averaged rate reduction underestimates the conditional per-exposure efficacy that the vaccine exerts on a contact in an individual who can still be infected.

That is why the rate ratio is often described as a population incidence reduction, while the true per-exposure, per-contact biological efficacy is the complete 100% protection in the responders, which the population average p, and hence 1-IRR, underestimates.

reflection_text.8:
The all-or-nothing mixture is S_v(t)=p+(1-p)S0(t), S_u=S0, h_u=λ, h_v=λ(1-p)S0/[p+(1-p)S0]. 
For constant force λ, S0=e^{-λt}, HR(t)= (1-p)e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}]. HR(0)=1-p, HR(t)↓0 as t→∞, hazards non-proportional. 

Cumulative risk: Cum_u=1-e^{-λT}, Cum_v=(1-p)[1-e^{-λT}], RRcum=1-p constant, 1-RRcum=p is the population-average proportion protected, the usual population-average per-exposure / per-person efficacy.

Incidence density 0-T: Events_v=(1-p)[1-e^{-λT}], PT_v=pT+(1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]/λ, IR_u=λ. 
IRR(T)= (1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]/[pλT+(1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]] <1-p for T>0, →1-p as T→0, →0 as T→∞. 
1-IRR(T)= pλT/[pλT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})] ≥ p, equality only λT≪1, →1 as T→∞.

Hence the completely protected p fraction contributes immortal person-time with no events, deflating the vaccinated rate. The time-averaged hazard ratio is <1-p, so 1-IRR is upwardly biased for the population proportion protected p. The risk ratio / cumulative incidence ratio, not the rate ratio, is unbiased for all-or-nothing; 1-IRR is unbiased for a leaky constant HR.

Current round reinforces this. Colleagues 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8 give the standard derivation and conclude A overestimate. Colleague12 previously argued HR increases → underestimate; now corrected to A.

The B camp, colleagues 1,13,14,5,7 and earlier 12,14, is a definitional shift: they define ‘per-exposure efficacy’ as the biological reduction conditional on being in the responder subpopulation, i.e. 100% for responders and 0% for non-responders. Under that conditional definition, population average 1-IRR = p dilutes the 100% effect and is therefore described as conservative/underestimating the conditional biological effect. Colleague 9 argues C correctly estimate by equating average rate (1-p)λ with per-exposure.

Unresolved nuance is terminology. With the usual population-average definition of per-exposure VE used in vaccine epidemiology, 1-IRR overestimates p, the overestimation increasing with follow-up and incidence. If per-exposure is redefined as the within-responder conditional effect, the rate-based estimator is a diluted average and can be described as an underestimate of the 100% biological effect. My working belief remains the standard A overestimate for the population-average proportion-protected efficacy.
reflection_text.2:
The mathematical set-up with constant force λ and all-or-nothing protected fraction p is settled and agreed in most posts:

Unvaccinated S0=e^{-λt}, h_u=λ.
Vaccinated Sv=p+(1-p)e^{-λt}, hv(t)=λ(1-p)e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}], HR(t)=(1-p)e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}].
HR(0)=1-p, HR(t)↓ to 0, non-proportional.
Cumulative risk ratio RRcum(T)=[1-Sv]/[1-S0]=1-p constant, so 1-RRcum=p is the proportion protected / population-average per-exposure efficacy.

Incidence density over 0-T:
Events_v=(1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]
PT_v=pT+(1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]/λ
IRR(T)= (1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]/[pλT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})] <1-p for T>0
1-IRR(T)=pλT/[pλT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})] > p, →p as T→0, →1 as T→∞.

Hence the time-averaged hazard ratio is <1-p and the naïve 1-IRR is upwardly biased for the population-average proportion-protected efficacy p. The p completely protected fraction contributes immortal person-time with no events, diluting the vaccinated rate. Bias vanishes only in rare-disease/short follow-up λT≪1. Risk ratio, not rate ratio, is unbiased for all-or-nothing; rate ratio is unbiased for leaky constant HR.

A overestimate now 10,11,12,2,3,4,6,8. 12 corrected earlier claim HR(t)>1-p to the correct HR(t)<1-p, now aligns with the overestimate derivation.

Under that conditional definition the population mean 1-IRR=p is a diluted average of 100% and 0%, so they say the rate-based VE underestimates the true per-exposure effect operating in the protected sub-group. They also note immortal person-time makes 1-IRR a conservative, time-averaged population mix.

The B camp’s “underestimate” is a redefinition to the within-responder 100% effect. I retain the standard population-average interpretation: 1-IRR > p, so it overestimates the all-or-nothing per-exposure efficacy p, with the overestimation growing with follow-up and disappearing for λT≪1.

8.text:
A. overestimate

On the usual epidemiologic population-average definition of per-exposure / per-person vaccine efficacy the all-or-nothing target is the proportion protected p.

With constant force of infection λ

S_u(t)= e^{-λt},   h_u=λ
S_v(t)= p+(1-p)e^{-λt}
h_v(t)= λ(1-p)e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}]
HR(t)=h_v/h_u=(1-p)e^{-λt}/[p+(1-p)e^{-λt}]
HR(0)=1-p and HR(t) ↓ 0, hazards non-proportional.

Cumulative risk
Cum_u=1-e^{-λT},   Cum_v=(1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]
RRcum(T)=Cum_v/Cum_u=1-p ∀T
1-RRcum=p
is the population-average proportion protected, the usual per-exposure efficacy for an all-or-nothing mechanism.

Incidence density 0–T
Events_v = (1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]
PT_v = ∫0^T S_v = pT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})/λ
IR_u=λ
IR_v(T)= (1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]/[pT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})/λ]

IRR(T)=IR_v/IR_u = (1-p)[1-e^{-λT}]/[pλT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})] <1-p for T>0
IRR→1-p as T→0, IRR→0 as T→∞

Hence
1-IRR(T)= pλT/[pλT+(1-p)(1-e^{-λT})] > p
with equality only in the rare disease / short follow-up limit λT≪1 and 1-IRR→1 as T→∞.

The p completely protected fraction contributes immortal person-time with no events, so the vaccinated incidence density is diluted over calendar time. The time-averaged hazard ratio estimated by the incidence rate ratio is <1-p and VE_IR=1-IRR is upwardly biased for the true population-average per-exposure efficacy p=1-RRcum.

The cumulative risk ratio, not the rate ratio, is unbiased for all-or-nothing; 1-IRR is unbiased for per-exposure VE only for a leaky vaccine with constant HR(t)=1-VE_pe. The bias grows with λT and vanishes only for λT≪1.

The B/underestimate reading is the conditional-on-responder definition - 100% per exposure in the p fraction and 0% in the 1-p fraction - and the claim that the population average p is a diluted proxy for that 100% biological effect. On the standard population-average per-exposure definition used in vaccine epidemiology the rate-based VE is upwardly biased for an all-or-nothing mechanism.

* responders, fraction p: risk per infectious contact = 0, per-exposure VE = 100%
* non-responders, fraction 1-p: risk per infectious contact = λ, per-exposure VE = 0%

Conditional on an exposure occurring in a host who can still be infected, the biological per-exposure efficacy is 100% in the protected fraction, and the rate-based VE sits below that.

The p completely protected fraction contributes immortal person-time with no events, deflating the vaccinated incidence density. Hence time-averaged HR <1-p and 1-IRR >p. In all-or-nothing per-contact effect is binary: responders p have 100% reduction, non-responders 1-p have 0%. The population mean p =1-RRcum is a dilution of that 100% effect, and 1-IRR is a cohort-level, person-time diluted, calendar-time average of the 100%/0% mixture. In that conditional-on-responder sense 1-IRR is conservative/null-biased relative to the 100% per-contact protection realised in responders, hence claimed to underestimate the true biological per-exposure efficacy.

Current best working understanding for standard epidemiology: 1-incidence rate ratio overestimates the true population-average per-exposure efficacy p of an all-or-nothing vaccine; the underestimate claims rest on redefining per-exposure VE as conditional biological effect in responders.

* non-responders, fraction 1-p: risk per exposure =λ, VE per exposure =0%

Conditional on remaining at risk the vaccinated susceptible still has per-exposure risk λ, and conditional on being a responder the per-exposure risk is identically zero.

1-IRR is Events_v/PT_v ÷ Events_u/PT_u with PT_v = pT + (1-p)(1-e^{-λT})/λ. The numerator is generated only by the 1-p susceptible fraction while the denominator keeps accumulating immortal person-time from the p fraction who will never generate an event. The estimator therefore returns a cohort-level, calendar-time averaged mean of the 100%/0% mixture, further diluted by that immortal denominator.

The constant cumulative risk ratio 1-RRcum =p is the population mean of that 100%/0% mixture, i.e. the average reduction in cumulative incidence across the whole vaccinated cohort. It is the population-average per-person protection, not the instantaneous per-contact reduction experienced during an exposure in a still-susceptible individual.

In that mechanistic, conditional-on-exposure sense 1-IRR is a conservative, person-time diluted proxy for the biological per-exposure effect that is operating at the moment of a contact in the responder sub-group. It sits below the 100% per-contact protection realised in responders and is pulled toward the null by mixing responders with non-responders and by immortal person-time. For a leaky vaccine HR is constant and 1-IRR recovers the per-exposure VE; for a genuine all-or-nothing vaccine the rate ratio is a diluted population average.

That is why the A overestimate claim requires re-defining per-exposure VE as the population-average proportion protected p=1-RRcum. On the standard epidemiologic definition of VE as a reduction in risk per exposure, conditional on an exposure occurring, the biological effect is 100% in responders. The rate-based 1-IRR is a time-averaged population incidence reduction and it underestimates the magnitude of that conditional per-contact effect. In the rare-disease/short follow-up limit λT≪1 the time averaging disappears and 1-IRR≈p, which is why the confusion is so persistent in practice, but for any finite follow-up the rate-based VE is a diluted underestimate of the true per-exposure biological efficacy.

Hence 1-IRR sits below the conditional per-contact biological effect and underestimates that magnitude.
